storyline.label: Diffusion Language
storyline.latest_title: SpecCTMC: Exact Speculative Simulation of Diffusion Language Model Continuous-Time Markov Chains

prior_narrative.tldr: Diffusion language models first surfaced here on the offensive side, as a way to craft fluent low-perplexity black-box attacks on LLMs. Two decoding-speed papers followed, cutting rounds via schedule distillation and adaptive compute for agents.
prior_narrative.whats_new: SpecCTMC proposes exact speculative simulation of masked diffusion LMs, keeping the output distribution intact while sampling multiple tokens in parallel; it follows length-extrapolation and multimodal hallucination papers.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Diffusion LLMs only pay off for serving if parallel decoding cuts rounds without changing output quality; SpecCTMC targets exactly that, but it is still research-stage evidence, not a deployable runtime.

status.detail: Six arXiv papers, no production release: attacks, decoding speed, length extrapolation and multimodal reliability.

beats.headline: Diffusion LMs used for perplexity-aware black-box attacks
Schedule distillation and metacognitive decoding aim to cut dLLM cost
Length extrapolation and multimodal hallucination expose weak spots

open_questions: Do the schedule-distillation, metacognitive-decoding and SpecCTMC speedups hold on independent benchmarks at equal output quality?
Does any inference framework or vendor ship diffusion LLM serving with parallel decoding?
Does RangeSWA's training-free extrapolation hold on long outputs beyond the paper's tested lengths?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Do not plan serving capacity around diffusion LLMs yet; if you prototype one, measure decoding rounds, output-distribution drift and quality against your autoregressive baseline, and include fluent-prompt attacks in red-team evals.

day_captions.4d1cef01d9ab5673: Uses a diffusion LM to generate low-perplexity attack prompts against black-box LLMs.
day_captions.75e015095613159e: Proposes learning when to commit tokens, reducing the decoding rounds dLLMs need.
day_captions.edcf9763d6b958dc: Extends the efficiency push to agents by adapting compute spent and text generated per interaction.
day_captions.581b8a72b6b37583: Training-free fix for repetition and quality loss when continuous diffusion LMs generate longer text.
day_captions.57b08f9866a26766: Targets hallucination in multimodal discrete diffusion LMs by ordering visual gain during mask prediction.
day_captions.2fb1a0f31494270f: Speculative simulation that preserves the exact output distribution when sampling several tokens in parallel.
